To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
force-induced changes in cytoplasmic binding to cytoskeletons occur in vivo and in vitro, and are mediated by paxillin and p130Cas.

the cytoskeleton of L-929 fibroblasts can be stretched in vitro by 10% without loss of integrity, and that stretch-dependent binding of several cytoplasmic focal adhesion proteins to the cytoskeleton is observed.
force-dependent conformational changes in the cytoskeleton can be transduced to the cytoplasm by binding of cytoplamsic proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which cells sense and respond to forces.
the molecular mechanisms of force transduction in the cellular cytoskeleton.
the molecular mechanisms of cell–matrix interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
force-induced changes in cytoskeleton structure can lead to conformational changes in cytoplasmic molecules that can then lead to signal transduction.
force-induced signal transduction is initiated by the binding of paxillins and other cytoskeleton-associated proteins to the cytoskeleton.
the cytoskeleton is an important force-transducing structure that is able to transduce mechanical signals from the ECM to the cell interior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
force-induced conformational changes in the cytoskeleton can initiate signaling pathways that regulate cell function.
the matrix is a dynamic force transducer that transmits mechanical signals to the cell via cytoplasmic and membrane-based mechanisms.
force transduction occurs via the cytoskeleton and that the cytoskeleton is the primary transducing structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoskeleton is a mechanosensory organelle.
the cytoskeleton is an active participant in force transduction, and not just the passive conduit for force transmission.
force transduction by the cytoskeleton is mediated by a complex network of proteins.
